answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation built like a trellis: each identity locks a refundable deposit and earns trust only through completed, peer-verified work. New identities enter through a narrow inlet of low-value tasks and reach higher-value jobs only after successful deliveries. A bridge between markets lets reputation travel only if verified. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must fund a deposit for each, do real work for each, and wait through the same slow ramp, so cost scales with every fake while payoff stays capped, making large sybil attacks unprofitable.
